title: OC Hypercar M1b: body fidelity
lensAText: a sceptical automotive art director. The owner's reference sheet was lost in the machine reset, so judge against the sheet's description, panel notes and measured numbers in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (sections on the sheet, the M1b row) and against HEAD (b49f7f3): look at every before/after render the builder cites with the Read tool, view by view (front, rear, side, three-quarter/hero, top, wheel): does it read as the car that file describes, honest about being a procedural model built in code, readable at phone size, clearly better than HEAD in every view the M1b row names, with no new artefacts? Take your own garage and chase-camera frames of the OC Hypercar at 390x844 and 1280x720 on dist/artifact.html, and confirm the other four cars are unchanged.
brief: OC Hypercar milestone M1b, body fidelity, as written in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (its M1b row: every numbered item, with the notes of what is done and not done) against the reference sheet that file names. The car is a procedural model built in code; our own brand (the OC mark); no real car brands or copied designs. HEAD is b49f7f3 (origin/claude/hypercar, the whole OC Hypercar). The first M1b build was judged: the ART lens KEPT it (clearly better than HEAD in every view the earlier art review had rejected; not yet a finished match to the sheet); the CODE lens REJECTED it: two items in the brief were still undone, and the reason given for one of them did not check out (the full verdicts were lost in the machine reset). A repair was in progress: its edits are restored on disk. Check EVERY M1b item; finish the undone ones; where an item truly needs a file that belongs to another session (src/preview/car-wheel.ts: e.g. the caliper's OC mark strip), do not edit it: say so plainly and give the exact change for that session, and make sure that reason is true. Nothing tied to the removed Races or Time Trial modes. PROVE: the same renders as M1 each beside its reference crop (front, rear, side, three-quarter, wheel) into tests/out/preview/m1b/; the other four cars' body geometry hashes identical to HEAD's and their lineup pixels identical; npx tsc --noEmit (tsconfig.json and tsconfig.game.json); npm run build; node tests/dynamics.mjs; npm test -- --only=boot,render,phone; the budget table in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md section 10 (triangles high and phone). UPDATE 2026-11-11 ~6:30 AM PT (second pass): the first post-reset builder finished the code and reported every item done except (a) the overlay/side-by-side against the reference sheet, because the owner's sheet (scratchpad/ref/hypercar-reference.png, 1774x887) was lost in the machine reset and is nowhere on the machine, (b) the rear's paint is no lighter than HEAD ((129,143,160) vs (134,149,165)), and (c) the render group never had one fully clean run at a load of ~23 (timeouts waiting 60 s for 5 frames; each check passed in some run). Its notes are in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md (the M1b row) and PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md. THIS PASS: the sheet-overlay proof is WAIVED because the file is gone (keep tests/out/preview/m1b/pairs.py so it can be rebuilt when the owner re-sends it): prove each view with before (HEAD b49f7f3) / after pairs instead and against the sheet's numbers recorded in PROJECT_OC_HYPERCAR.md; do not report done=false for that alone. Lift the rear's paint toward the sheet's light silver as item 9 asks (a median clearly lighter than HEAD in the rear view, without changing the other four cars). Get ONE fully clean 'npm test -- --only=render' run of the final code: run it when the machine is least busy (check 'uptime'; other lanes may finish soon), never weaken a check or raise its timeouts. Re-shoot every frame you cite (earlier frames in tests/out/preview/m1b/ may be stale). Report done=true when the work is ready for review, listing honestly anything still not met.
